triggers.name: api
triggers.note: A request to the one HTTPS function `api`. Every command the Svelte app sends lands here — and the REST API and MCP server (Platform) reach the same handlers through their own middleware.

triggers.name: firestore
triggers.note: A document changed under it and it ran. Used only for derived data: search index, rollups, counts.

triggers.name: auth
triggers.note: An account was created or deleted, by any provider.

triggers.name: queue
triggers.note: A Cloud Tasks queue — retried with backoff, rate-limited, deduplicated by task name.

triggers.name: module
triggers.note: Not reached from outside: logic other code imports.

middleware.name: user
middleware.note: A Firebase ID token, from the Svelte app.
code: // AUTHORIZATION IS NOT HERE. Who you are is a token fact; what
// you may do is a BOARD fact, answered per command by can() after
// the board is loaded — the reference tracker's loadBoardWithRole
// + requireMin, which was the right shape.

proxyFunctions.name: can
proxyFunctions.location: one question: may this actor do this to this board?
ioSchema: function can(ctx, board: Board, action: Action, ticket?: Ticket, toStageId?: string): boolean
// ctx.actor is a PRINCIPAL: a uid, or an agent id when a token acts as an agent
implementation: role = effectiveRole(board, ctx.actor)   // board.access[actor]; an agent's 'admin' reads as editor
if !role → false   // not on the board: nothing, not even read
if ctx.scopes && !scopeAllows(ctx.scopes, action) → false
if ctx.boardIds && board.id not in ctx.boardIds  → false
admin:     everything, including inviting, removing and re-roling people
editor:    everything but 'admin' and 'restore'
commenter: read, comment, upload, and 'move' IF
grant = board.stageGrants[actor]
from ∈ grant.stages && to ∈ grant.stages
&& (!grant.assignedOnly || actor ∈ ticket.assigneeUids)
viewer:    read
'delete' additionally needs board.settings.allowDelete, and no token
scope grants it — hard delete is app-only.
SCOPES → ACTIONS (ACTION_SCOPES): comment/pin ← comments:write,
create ← tickets:create, edit ← tickets:update, move ← tickets:move,
assign ← tickets:assign, state/restore ← tickets:state,
upload ← files:write, admin ← board:admin | webhooks:manage.
WHAT A TOKEN MAY DO = its scopes ∩ what its principal's role allows.
An agent that is a commenter never moves a ticket outside its
StageGrant, whatever its token says. People and agents take exactly
the same path through here — there is no agent branch to forget.
ONE LOOKUP, ONE ROLE, ONE BOARD. Nothing above the board can grant
anything on it.
PURE AND UNIT-TESTED, like the reference's _tt-role.ts.

proxyFunctions.name: allocateKey
ioSchema: function allocateKey(tx, board): { key: TicketKey, number: number }
implementation: n = board.nextNumber
tx.update(board, { nextNumber: n + 1 })
tx.create(keys/{board.key}-{n}, { ticketId, boardId, current })
A COUNTER ON THE BOARD DOCUMENT, not a query for max(number). The
board doc can take ~1 sustained write/sec, which is one new ticket
per second on one board — a bulk import uses allocateRange(n).

proxyFunctions.name: parseRichText
proxyFunctions.location: every body that arrives from any door
implementation: validate doc against the TipTap schema   // unknown node → 400
strip marks not in the allow-list        // no raw HTML, ever
mentions = mention nodes whose uid is on this board (members/)
refs     = ticketRef nodes on boards the AUTHOR can read
text     = plain-text render ('@Priya Shah', '#ENG-42')
Markdown arriving from REST / MCP / email is converted to the same doc
first. A mention there is written as an EMAIL — '@priya@x.com' or
[@Priya](mailto:priya@x.com) — and resolved to that person's uid on
this board; an email not on the board stays plain text.

proxyFunctions.name: rank
proxyFunctions.location: ordering inside a column or a list
ioSchema: function between(a: string | null, b: string | null): string
implementation: fractional-indexing: a string strictly between a and b
A DRAG WRITES ONE DOCUMENT. Integer positions would renumber the
whole column on every drop — N writes, N snapshot events, N
chances to race another person dragging in the same column.

proxyFunctions.name: notify
proxyFunctions.location: every event, every channel — one router
ioSchema: function notify(event: NotifyEvent, ticket: Ticket, ctx, extra?: {
messageId?: string, mentioned?: PrincipalId[], changes?: object,
unassigned?: PrincipalId[]      // phase 2: agents get an 'unassigned' event
implementation: candidates = watchers ∪ assignees ∪ board readers   (board-wide events)
| mentioned                              ('mentioned' — unconditional)
drop the actor — never notify yourself (a person OR an agent)
split by principalKind(id):
PEOPLE, as before:
pref = prefs/{uid}  — mode (all | mine | muted) / events / stageIds as the
reference's boardRecipients(); watching overrides
channels = user.notify.channels[event]
write users/{uid}/inbox (collapsed by groupKey)       — always, if pref allows
enqueue deliver/{uid}:{groupKey}:{minute}            — push / email / whatsapp
AGENTS (phase 2) — no prefs, no channels, no delivery:
only if assigned to or watching the ticket, or mentioned
event ∈ assigned | unassigned | mentioned | comment | stage | updated | created
write agentInbox/{agentId}/events/{agentEventId(now, suffix)}
{ type, boardId, ticketId, ticketKey, messageId?, actor, summary, ackedAt: null }
NOT collapsed: each is a thing for the orchestrator to handle
ENQUEUED, NOT SENT. The command returns before any channel is
touched. The reference fired email as void-promises from the
handler — a cold SMTP connection then counted against the request,
and a crash lost the mail. A queue retries and deduplicates.
AGENTS GET AN INBOX, NOT A PUSH. An orchestrator is a program: it
polls, streams or acks; it has no phone. Board webhooks keep working
for orchestrators that want push.

proxyFunctions.name: diff
proxyFunctions.location: what changed, as activity and as notification copy
ioSchema: function diff(before: Ticket, after: Ticket): Record<string, { from, to }>
implementation: compare the fields a person would call a change —
title, description, stage, priority, tags, assignees, dates,
estimate, fields.*, links
ignore derived ones — counts, rank, lastActivityAt, updatedAt

services.name: inviteCreate
ioSchema: invites: { email: string, role: BoardRole }[]   // up to 50
interface Res { invited: string[], alreadyOnBoard: string[] }
implementation: can(admin) — or editor, when board.settings.editorsCanInvite
for each email (lower-cased):
a user with this email already on the board → alreadyOnBoard
a pending invite exists → refreshed, not duplicated
token = random(32); create invites/{id} with sha256(token)
enqueue email 'invite': '<Priya> invited you to <Engineering> as editor'
a user with this email exists → also an inbox item 'invited'
ANYONE CAN BE INVITED — they need not have an account. They sign up
with that address and the invite is waiting in their inbox.
OPEN SIGN-UP MEANS ANYONE CAN SEND MAIL THROUGH US. So: 50 invites per
person per day, 10 new boards per person per day (rateLimits), and an
invite email names the inviter's verified address — never a free-text sender.

services.name: inviteAccept
ioSchema: token?: string        // from the email link; absent when accepting from the inbox
interface Res { boardId: BoardId, boardKey: BoardKey }
implementation: invite pending && not expired                    → 410 otherwise
token given: sha256(token) == tokenHash          → 404 otherwise
auth email (verified) == invite.email            → 403 otherwise
THE ACCEPTING ACCOUNT MUST OWN THE INVITED ADDRESS. A forwarded link
is the most common way access goes to the wrong person.
decline → status 'declined'; the inviter is told
accept, in one transaction:
board.access[uid] = role; readerUids / editorUids += uid
create boards/{b}/members/{uid} from users/{uid}
invite.status = 'accepted'
then: RTDB boardReaders mirror; notify inviter 'Asha joined Engineering'
FROM HERE THEY CAN BE ASSIGNED, MENTIONED AND NOTIFIED on this board —
and only on this board.

services.name: inviteRevoke
implementation: can(admin) on the invite's board (or its inviter)
resend → new token, new expiry, the email again
otherwise status = 'revoked'; the link and the inbox row stop working

services.name: boardCreate
implementation: ANY signed-in user may create a board
transaction:
create boardKeys/{key}   → 409 if taken
create boards/{b}        from the template; access = { [actor]: 'admin' }; readerUids = [actor]
create boards/{b}/members/{actor}
create default views: Board (kanban by stage), Table, Calendar, Mine
template { fromBoardId } copies stages, fields and views — never people

services.name: boardUpdate
ioSchema: // removing a stage in use needs somewhere to put its tickets:
remap?: { stages?: Record<string, string>, priorities?: Record<string, string> }
implementation: can(admin)
a removed stage with tickets and no remap → 409 { stageId, count }
a removed field is ARCHIVED, never deleted — values stay
a stage whose category changed → batch-update stageCategory on its tickets
PATCHES ARE PER-SECTION, not a whole SETTINGS blob. The reference's
PATCH replaced settings wholesale and had to carry `reporting`
through by hand so a normal save could not wipe the secret.

services.name: tagCreate
ioSchema: interface Req { boardId, name: string, color?: string }
implementation: can(edit) — editors make tags on the fly from the picker, as in the reference;
renaming, recolouring and deleting tags stays with admins (boardUpdate)
same name, any case → the existing tag is returned (the reference's rule)

services.name: boardAccessSet
ioSchema: people?: Record<Uid, BoardRole | null>          // change a role; null removes them — PEOPLE only
implementation: can(admin), except 'leave', which anyone may do
at least one admin must remain → 409 otherwise
a removed person:
access / readerUids / members/{uid} removed
taken off assigneeUids and watcherUids of the board's active tickets
(listed in each ticket's activity), and told
their messages stay
new people are never added here — only through inviteCreate / inviteAccept
an agent id in people / stageGrants → 400: agents go through boardAgentSet
a removed person's tokens for this board are revoked (revokedReason 'ownerLeft')

services.name: boardAgentSet
ioSchema: role: 'editor' | 'commenter' | 'viewer' | null   // null removes the agent; never 'admin'
stageGrant?: StageGrant | null                  // commenters; absent = unchanged
implementation: ADDING (not on the board yet): can(admin) AND the actor OWNS the agent,
agent not archived → 403 / 404 / 409 otherwise
CHANGING or REMOVING: any board admin — an admin must be able to take
someone else's agent off their board
transaction:
board.access[agentId] = role, stageGrants[agentId] = grant
readerUids / editorUids untouched — agents are never in them
members/{agentId} = { kind: 'agent', uid: agentId, role, stageGrant,
name, avatarPath, icon, description, ownerUid, addedBy: actor,
email: '', invitedBy: null, joinedAt }
role: null — works like removing a person:
access / stageGrants / members/{agentId} removed
taken off assigneeUids and watcherUids of the board's active tickets
(listed in each ticket's activity); its messages stay
its tokens for this board → revoked, revokedReason 'agentRemoved'
NO INVITE. An agent has nobody to accept for it, and the person who
could accept is the admin adding it. Webhook 'member.joined' fires
with actor.kind 'agent'.

services.name: agentInboxAck
ioSchema: upTo?: string       // an event id / cursor: ack everything ≤ it
interface Res { ok: true, acked: number }
implementation: the agent's owner (app), or a token acting as that agent (scope events:read)
ackedAt = now on the named events, or on every event with id ≤ upTo
acking twice is ok — acked counts only the ones that changed
ACK IS NOT DELETE. The orchestrator's cursor already says what it has
seen; ack says what it has HANDLED, so a crashed run can re-read
?unacked=1 and pick up where it died. Acked events are TTL-deleted
after 30 days.

services.name: boardArchive
ioSchema: interface Req { boardId, action: 'archive' | 'restore' | 'delete', confirmKey?: BoardKey }
implementation: can(admin)
archive: archivedAt = now — read-only for everyone, off the sidebar, under 'Archived' on Boards
restore: archivedAt = null
delete: confirmKey must equal the key; queued recursive delete of tickets, threads, files;
the key stays claimed (keys/ and boardKeys/ kept as tombstones) so old #links say 'deleted'

services.name: boardPrefSet
ioSchema: interface Req { boardId, pref: Partial<BoardPref> }   // always the caller's own
implementation: can(read) on the board
writes prefs/{actor} — there is no uid parameter: nobody sets another person's
The reference's owner-managed mode (notify_pref_control) is dropped.

services.name: viewSave
ioSchema: interface Req { boardId, viewId?, view: Omit<View, 'ownerUid'> }
implementation: personal → can(read); shared → can(edit)
validate filter fields exist on the board (a view naming a
deleted field would silently match nothing)

services.name: viewDelete
implementation: personal → its owner; shared → can(edit)
the board's default view cannot be deleted (choose another default first)
prefs whose lastViewId pointed at it fall back to the default

services.name: ticketCreate
ioSchema: stageId?: string          // default: the board's first stage BY POSITION (§Q3)
attachments?: string[]    // Storage paths already uploaded
clientId?: string         // idempotency — a retried create is one ticket
interface Res { ticketId: TicketId, key: TicketKey }
implementation: can(create)
validate stage / priority / tags / fields against the board
required fields present
assignees: every principal (person or agent) is on this board (members/) — else 400, naming them
description = parseRichText(description)
transaction:
{ key } = allocateKey(board)
create ticket { …, rank: between(last in stage, null), watcherUids:
[actor, …assignees], createdVia: ctx.via }
after commit:
notify('created'), notify('assigned', assignees),
notify('mentioned', description.mentions)
emit webhook 'ticket.created'
memoryRefs (plan/memory.html §E): memory files by reference — the memory must be granted to this board; rows source 'memory', path memories/{m}/nodes/{n}

services.name: ticketUpdate
ioSchema: patch: Partial<{ title, description, stageId, priorityId, tagIds,
rank?: { after?: TicketId, before?: TicketId }   // drag & drop
ifUpdatedAt?: Millis    // optimistic concurrency for the title/description
implementation: state != 'active' → 409 (read-only, as in the reference)
only stageId (+rank) changing and !can(edit) → can(move, to)
otherwise can(edit); assigneeUids changing → can(assign)
a token needs EVERY scope patchScopes(patch) names: stageId → tickets:move,
assigneeUids → tickets:assign, anything else → tickets:update
ifUpdatedAt given and stale → 409 with the current ticket
transaction:
apply patch; stageCategory follows stageId;
completedAt set/cleared on entering/leaving 'done'
activity { changes: diff(before, after), viaGrant }
after commit: notify('stage' | 'updated' | 'assigned', unassigned), webhook 'ticket.updated'
FIELD-LEVEL MERGE, not last-write-wins on the document: two people
changing the priority and the due date at once both land.
links: a 'blocks' on A writes 'blockedBy' on B in the same transaction
(and 'relates'/'duplicates' both ways); activity 'link' on both
stage 'requires' unmet → 422 { missing: fieldIds } — the UI opens a small
form for exactly those fields instead of snapping the card back

services.name: ticketBulk
ioSchema: interface Res { updated: number, skipped: TicketId[] }
implementation: the reference's POST_TtBoardTasksBulk: the board and role are
resolved once; a commenter may only run 'stage', over the tickets
their grant covers — the rest are SKIPPED and reported, not failed
batched writes of 250 (ticket + activity each)
ONE digest notification per recipient ('Priya moved 14 tickets to Done')
rather than fourteen

services.name: ticketState
implementation: active → archived : can(state)     // PHASE 6: no 'cancelled', no reason
archived → active : can(restore)   // admin, as in the reference
activity + system message + notify('state')

services.name: ticketDelete
implementation: board.settings.allowDelete && can(delete)

recursive delete: ticket, messages, activity, files, Storage prefix;
remove it from the links / referencedBy of the tickets that pointed at it
keys/{key} kept with { deleted: true } so #ENG-42 says 'deleted'
rather than 'not found' — and is never reissued

services.name: messagePost
ioSchema: markdown?: string           // phase 2: the Markdown source (REST / MCP doors); stored as Message.markdown
attachments?: string[]      // Storage paths under this ticket (the app's direct uploads)
fileIds?: string[]          // phase 2: files ALREADY on this ticket (uploaded by a token)
clientId: string            // idempotency; the optimistic bubble's id
implementation: can(comment); state == 'active' (closed tickets have closed threads)
body = parseRichText(body)
attachments: object exists, under this ticket's prefix, size/mime ok
fileIds: files/{id} on THIS ticket, not deleted; source 'upload' → 'message', messageId set
body or files, at least one — a message can be files only
authorUid = ctx.actor (a person or an agent); viaToken = ctx.keyName
transaction:
create message; create files/* for each attachment (source 'message')
ticket.counts.messages++, attachments += n, lastMessageAt = now
ticket.refs ∪= body.refs; watcherUids ∪= [actor]
reads/{actor} = now          // your own message is read
after commit:
notify('mentioned', body.mentions)      // unconditional
notify('comment') minus those mentioned // no double ping

for each NEW #ref: target.referencedBy += this ticket, and a system line
  on THAT ticket: 'referenced from ENG-40'
webhook 'message.created'
memoryRefs (plan/memory.html §E): memory files by reference — the memory must be granted to this board; rows source 'memory', path memories/{m}/nodes/{n}

services.name: messageEdit
ioSchema: interface Req { messageId, body?: RichText['doc'], delete?: true }
implementation: author only (admins may delete, not edit)
edit: editedAt = now; NEW mentions notify, old ones do not again
delete: tombstone — body cleared, deletedAt set, attachments removed
delete also stamps deletedAt on that message's files/

services.name: messagePin
implementation: can(pin) = editor+ (the reference gated pin on 'edit')
pinnedAt/pinnedBy set or cleared; ticket.counts.pinned ±1
system message 'Priya pinned a message' — pins are decisions,
and who made one belongs in the thread

services.name: questionAsk
ioSchema: title: string               // 'Which database should the report use?'
fields: QuestionField[]     // 1–10; single / multi carry their options
to?: PrincipalId[] | null   // who should answer; null = anyone who may comment
clientId: string            // IS the message id — the card's thread position
interface Res { messageId: string, questionId: string }   // '{ticketId}.{messageId}'
implementation: can(ask) — commenter+, normally an agent's token with questions:write
the ticket must be active (a closed thread takes no questions → 409)
`to` must name principals ON the board, or the card waits forever (400)
transaction:
the message: kind 'question', the form in `question`, body = title +
context so search, previews and the notification line read it
ticket counts.messages++, lastMessageAt, watcherUids ∪= asker
ticket.waitingOn when the question blocks   // the ❓ badge on cards
after commit:
notify('question') to the `to` people — or, when it names nobody, the
assignees and watchers — through their normal channels
webhook 'message.created', carrying the form card

services.name: questionAnswer
services.location: POST /api/questionAnswer   // a PERSON answers, in the app
ioSchema: comment?: string            // only when the question has allowComment
clientId: string            // Submit goes through the outbox like any write
interface Res { ok: true, answeredAt: Millis }
implementation: canAnswerQuestion(): commenter+, and in `to` when it is set; the question
still open at now (409 answered / cancelled / expired)
values checked by the SHARED validateAnswer — the browser disables Submit
for the same reason the server answers 422
transaction:
the card locks in place: question.status 'answered' + the answer
the answer ALSO posts as the person's reply bubble (replyTo = the card)
ticket counters; ticket.waitingOn recomputed when it was blocking
after commit: the ASKING AGENT's inbox event 'question_answered', carrying
the values — an orchestrator needs no second call to act on it.
THERE IS NO answer_question TOOL. An agent asks; a person answers.

services.name: questionCancel
ioSchema: interface Req { ticketId: TicketId, messageId: string, clientId: string }
implementation: the ASKER (the message author, usually the agent through its token) or a
board admin; open questions only (409 otherwise)
transaction: question.status 'cancelled' + cancelledAt; ticket.waitingOn
recomputed. No thread line — the card itself says it.
after commit: 'question_cancelled' to the asking agent, but only when
somebody ELSE cancelled it (§D: an agent never hears its own actions).

services.name: tasklistSet
ioSchema: listId?: string             // absent = create; present = create-or-replace THAT list
items: { id?, title, status?, note? }[]    // ≤ 100 — the WHOLE list
closed?: boolean            // true = the plan is finished
interface Res { listId: string, itemIds: string[] }
implementation: canEditTasklist(): editor+, or the list's OWNER (a commenter agent through
its token with tasklists:write). Creating sets owner = actor; replacing
keeps the owner it has. The ticket must be active.
WHOLE-LIST WRITES, so an agent republishing its plan never has to diff it.
An item keeps its id — and its updatedAt when nothing about it changed —
so a replace does not make every row look touched.
transaction:
the list document
ticket.tasklistProgress rolled up over EVERY list on the ticket ('4/7')
a system line when the list is CREATED, and one when it is FINISHED
— never for an item (§L2: 'to keep the thread readable')

services.name: tasklistItemUpdate
ioSchema: ticketId: TicketId, listId: string, itemId: string
note?: string | null        // null clears it
interface Res { ok: true, updatedAt: Millis }
implementation: canEditTasklist() on the STORED list. THE HOT PATH: an agent calls this as
it works, and a person ticking a box by hand goes through the same command.
No activity row and no thread line. The one exception is the list
FINISHING: when this tick settles the last item the list closes and the
second (and last) system line goes out.
ticket.tasklistProgress is rolled up again — the card's chip is the only
thing on the board that has to notice.

services.name: tasklistDelete
ioSchema: interface Req { ticketId: TicketId, listId: string, clientId: string }
implementation: canEditTasklist() on the stored list — editor+, or its owner.
Silent: no thread line, no activity row. The ticket's chip is recomputed
from the lists that remain (none left → no chip).
The only 'delete' anywhere in the API removes a CHECKLIST, never a ticket.

services.name: agentHeartbeat
ioSchema: ticketId?: TicketId         // absent = an agent-level beat, about no ticket
agentId?: AgentId           // absent = ctx.actor (an agent token IS the agent)
interface Res { ok: true, statusId: string, at: Millis }
implementation: canHeartbeat(): a token acting as the agent (or a board admin) with
status:write; the agent must hold a role on the board.
WRITES EXACTLY ONE SMALL DOCUMENT — boards/{b}/agentStatus/{id} — and
NEVER the ticket. A beat a minute on the ticket would retrigger its search
indexing and re-render every listener on the board.
startedAt  the first beat of THIS run; reset when 'working' follows a
done / error beat
endedAt    set by 'done' / 'error', cleared when work resumes
silenceNotifiedAt  left alone: a fresh lastBeatAt re-arms the sweep
Nothing is notified. The beat is read, not pushed: the board's one
agentStatus listener turns it into a dot.

services.name: messageReact
ioSchema: interface Req { messageId, emoji: string, on: boolean }
implementation: can(comment); arrayUnion/arrayRemove on reactions[emoji]
no notification — a reaction is not a message

services.name: ticketWatch
implementation: watcherUids ± actor; prefs/{actor}.watching ± ticketId
the reference's 'subscribe' — overrides a muted board

services.name: searchKey
ioSchema: interface Res { key: string, host: string, expiresAt: Millis }
implementation: boards = where(readerUids array-contains actor)
key = typesense.generateScopedSearchKey(searchOnlyKey,
{ filter_by: `boardId:[${boards}]`, expires_at: +1h })

services.name: profileUpdate
ioSchema: avatarPath?: string | null  // just uploaded to users/{uid}/avatar/…; null removes it
implementation: avatarPath: must be under users/{actor}/avatar/, exist, and be an image
update users/{actor}; the previous picture is deleted
name or avatar changed → collectionGroup('members') where uid == actor
→ update name / avatarPath on every board they're on
Mentions and assignees hold the uid, so nothing else is rewritten —
they render the new name and picture on their own.
EMAIL IS NOT HERE. It is the sign-in identity; changing it goes through
Firebase Auth's verify-new-email flow, and a trigger copies the verified
address to users/ and members/.

services.name: agentCreate
ioSchema: agentId?: AgentId          // optional client-made 'ag_…' id, so the picture can be
icon?: string | null       // a prebuilt icon id (AGENT_ICON_IDS); unknown → 400
implementation: any signed-in person; they become its owner
50 agents per person → 429
agentId given and taken → 409
avatarPath: under users/{actor}/agents/{agentId}/avatar/, exists, image
create agents/{agentId} { ownerUid: actor, …, archivedAt: null }
APP-ONLY. No token scope reaches the agent commands: a token acts AS
an agent, it never manages one.

services.name: agentUpdate
ioSchema: icon?: string | null       // a prebuilt icon id (AGENT_ICON_IDS); null clears it, the picture stays
implementation: owner only — 404 otherwise (agents are private; not even 403)
archived → 409
update agents/{agentId}; a replaced picture is deleted
name or avatar changed → collectionGroup('members') where uid == agentId
→ update name / avatarPath / icon / description on every board it is on
THE SAME FAN-OUT AS profileUpdate. Assignees, mentions and authors
hold the id, so they render the new name and picture on their own.
A new system prompt reaches the orchestrator the next time it asks
(GET /v1/me, MCP whoami) — nothing is pushed.

services.name: agentArchive
ioSchema: interface Req { agentId: AgentId, action?: 'archive' | 'restore' }   // default 'archive'
interface Res { ok: true, boardsLeft: number, tokensRevoked: number }
implementation: owner only (404 otherwise)
archive:
every board it is on → boardAgentSet(role: null): off access, members,
assignees and watchers; its messages stay
every apiKey acting as it → revokedAt = now, revokedReason 'agentArchived'
archivedAt = now
restore: archivedAt = null. It rejoins no board and no token comes
back — both were decisions, and restoring should not re-make them.
ARCHIVE, NOT DELETE: its name and picture still have to render on
every message it wrote.

services.name: whatsappLink
ioSchema: interface Req { step: 'send', number: string } | { step: 'verify', code: string }
implementation: send:   6-digit code via the WhatsApp 'otp' template; hash stored 10 min
verify: 5 attempts; users/{uid}.whatsapp = { number, verifiedAt, optIn: true }
OPT-IN IS EXPLICIT AND RECORDED. Meta requires it before any
business-initiated template, and it is the only defence when a
number is reported.

services.name: accountDelete
implementation: the only admin of a board that has other people on it → 409, naming the boards
(make someone else admin, or delete the board)
leave every board (boardAccessSet leave)
archive every agent they own (agentArchive) — its messages stay
boards where they were the only person → deleted
users/{uid}: name → 'Deleted user', email/phone/avatar cleared,
deletedAt = now; picture deleted
messages STAY, authored by 'Deleted user' — deleting them would
rewrite other people's conversations
admin.auth().deleteUser(uid)

services.name: accountExport
ioSchema: interface Res { jobId: string }  // emailed when ready
implementation: queued: profile, messages authored, tickets created/assigned → JSON + files → zip in Storage
signed URL valid 7 days, emailed

services.name: onUserCreated
implementation: users/{uid} = { name and email from the provider, timezone from the client's
first call, notify: defaults }
the provider's photo (Google) is copied into users/{uid}/avatar/ so the
picture never depends on a third-party URL
pending invites for this (verified) email → an inbox item each
NO GATE. Anyone may sign up; a new account simply has no boards until
it creates one or accepts an invite.

services.name: onUserSignedIn
ioSchema: // runs on every sign-in, before the token is issued
implementation: email or email_verified differs from users/{uid}.email →
update users/{uid}.email and every boards/*/members/{uid}.email
HOW AN EMAIL CHANGE REACHES THE DATA. Firebase has no 'email changed'
trigger; the next sign-in after a verified change is the first moment we
can see it, and the token it mints carries the new address anyway.

services.name: onTicketWritten
ioSchema: // derived data only — never business rules
implementation: upsert / delete the Typesense document
board.counts (active / done / overdue) via FieldValue.increment
IDEMPOTENT BY EVENT ID. Firestore triggers are at-least-once; a
counter bumped twice is a board that says 41 when there are 40.

services.name: onMessageWritten
implementation: fold the ticket's last 20 message texts into its Typesense document,
so search finds a ticket by something said in its thread

services.name: onAttachmentFinalized
implementation: sharp → webp thumbnail, metadata width/height
(phase 3) ClamAV on Cloud Run for non-images; infected → quarantined
unattached after 24h → deleted by attachmentSweep
users/*/avatar/* → cropped square, 256px webp; the original is replaced

services.name: deadlineSweep
ioSchema: // collection-group: tickets where state == 'active' && dueAt <= now + 72h
// (72h = the longest lead time anyone may choose)
implementation: for each ticket not in a 'done' stage, for each assignee:
lead = users/{uid}.notify.dueSoonLeadMinutes
dueAt - now ≤ lead && !dueNotified[uid].soon → notify('dueSoon', to: uid)
dueAt < now && !dueNotified[uid].overdue    → notify('overdue', to: uid)
dueNotified IS PER PERSON AND MAKES A RE-RUN HARMLESS. Changing dueAt
clears it, so a moved deadline warns again.
commitments[uid] passed and commitmentReminders → a nudge to THAT person
board.counts.overdue recomputed for every board touched — time makes a
ticket overdue, and no write would ever notice

services.name: agentSilenceSweep
ioSchema: // plus: question messages whose expiresAt has passed (§L1)
implementation: THE PHASE-3 MINUTE TICK — two sweeps ride on it because both must happen
within about a minute of their deadline and neither is worth a schedule.
silence: a 'working' agent quiet for 5 minutes → ONE inbox row for its
OWNER, event 'agentSilence' ('Builder stopped reporting on ENG-42 — no
signal for 6 min'), then silenceNotifiedAt = now so it is said ONCE per
silence. An archived agent is not running: nobody is told.
The DOT does not need this — the UI derives 'No signal' from the clock.
expiry: a question past its expiresAt locks as 'Expired' and the ticket's
waitingOn is recomputed, so the ❓ badge goes away by itself.

services.name: digestSend
ioSchema: // users whose local time is 09:00 (daily) or anyone with hourly digest
implementation: unread inbox items since the last digest, grouped by board
+ 'due today' and 'overdue' from My Work
one email; nothing to say → nothing sent

services.name: housekeeping
ioSchema: // the jobs nobody should have to remember
implementation: invites past expiresAt → 'expired'
inbox items older than 90 days and read → deleted
boards with autoArchiveDoneAfterDays → archive done tickets
unattached uploads older than 24h → deleted
webhook deliveries older than 30 days → deleted

services.name: workspaceCreate
ioSchema: interface Req { name, color?, boardIds?, artifactIds? }
implementation: ≤ 50 workspaces per person
every boardId: I am a member (archived allowed); every artifactId: I have a role
duplicates dropped, order kept

services.name: workspaceUpdate
ioSchema: interface Req { workspaceId, name?, color?, boardIds?, artifactIds?, position? }
implementation: my own workspace only
the same reachability check as workspaceCreate for any new id

services.name: workspaceDelete
implementation: my own workspace only; its boards and artifacts are untouched

services.name: sidebarHide
ioSchema: interface Req { kind: 'board' | 'artifact', id, hidden: boolean }
implementation: UI only: never archives, never changes access
an id I cannot reach is refused

services.name: artifactBoardAccessSet
ioSchema: interface Req { artifactId, boardId, access: 'read' | 'write' | null }
implementation: artifact OWNER only; I must be on the board
'write' needs me to be editor or above on that board
the grant is a ceiling: each viewer still reaches only what their own board role allows (plan/artifacts.html §K)

services.name: memoryCreate
implementation: any allowed person (never an agent or a board token); ≤ 100 owned
they become its owner

services.name: memoryUpdate
ioSchema: interface Req { memoryId, name?, description?, icon?, archived? }
implementation: owner only; archived = read-only for everyone until restored

services.name: memoryDelete
implementation: owner only
ONE write empties access and grants and stamps deletingAt (unreachable at once)
queue memoryDelete: Storage prefix, nodes, the document last

services.name: memoryShare
ioSchema: interface Req { memoryId, email, role: 'editor' | 'viewer' | null }
implementation: owner only, never an agent
the person must already have an account (409 noAccount otherwise)

services.name: memoryGrantSet
ioSchema: interface Req { memoryId, boardId? | artifactId?, access: 'read' | 'write' | null }
implementation: memory owner AND board admin (or artifact owner)
null removes; ≤ 20 boards and 20 artifacts

services.name: memoryList
ioSchema: interface Res { memories: { id, name, reach, stats, … }[] }
implementation: own memories ∪ those granted to boards the caller is on
each with the caller's reach

services.name: memoryTree
implementation: read reach; nodes under path, sorted

services.name: memoryFileRead
ioSchema: interface Req { memoryId, path | nodeId, asText? }
interface Res { node, text, truncated, url, bytesUrl, expiresAt }
implementation: read reach; text ≤ 1 MB for text files; the file door's signed URLs

services.name: memoryFileWrite
ioSchema: interface Req { memoryId, path | nodeId, text | content_base64, mime?, expectedFileId? }
implementation: write reach; ≤ 10 MB; parents created
a NEW object, the node points at it, the old object is deleted after commit (D-M2)
expectedFileId ≠ current → 409 stale

services.name: memoryFilePut
ioSchema: interface Req { memoryId, path | nodeId, storagePath, expectedFileId? }
implementation: write reach; the object the app uploaded under memories/{m}/{fileId}/{name}
size and type from the object; one object never backs two nodes

services.name: memoryFolderCreate
implementation: write reach; mkdir -p; an existing folder is fine, a file in the way is 409

services.name: memoryMove
ioSchema: interface Req { memoryId, path | nodeId, toPath }
implementation: write reach; parents created; a folder takes its subtree
409 onto something, or a folder into itself

services.name: memoryNodeDelete
implementation: write reach; recursive; counters follow; objects deleted after
